title: Inter Milan open talks with Tottenham over Cristian Romero
dek: Inter Milan have initiated negotiations with Tottenham regarding a potential transfer of captain Cristian Romero, according to reporting by ESPN and Press Association on July 26. Romero's representatives were in Milan over the weekend for talks with Inter sporting director Piero Ausilo, who confirmed the club's interest while cautioning that deal-making requires time.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Inter Milan sporting director Piero Ausilo confirmed on-record that the club is in talks with Tottenham over Romero's signature, stating: 'It's definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club (Tottenham). These things take some time but there's definitely interest.'
bottom_line: Ausilo's confirmation that Inter is actively pursuing Romero suggests serious intent, but his emphasis on the time required for such negotiations suggests the clubs remain distant on fee and terms. Watch for updates on whether Romero's representatives and Tottenham move closer to an agreement in the coming weeks, and whether other clubs enter the race to complicate Inter's path.
body: Inter Milan have entered negotiations with Tottenham over the potential transfer of captain Cristian Romero, according to reporting by ESPN and Press Association on July 26. The discussions mark a significant move in the European transfer window, with Romero's representatives in Milan over the weekend for talks with Inter sporting director Piero Ausilo.

Romero, 28, is a World Cup finalist who helped Argentina reach a second straight World Cup final earlier this month. At Tottenham, he has made 156 appearances since joining in 2021 and guided the club to Europa League success last year while serving as captain under manager Roberto De Zerbi.

Ausilo confirmed the club's interest on record, stating: "It's definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club (Tottenham). These things take some time but there's definitely interest. Let's see." Tottenham has signaled willingness to let Romero depart this summer for a significant fee following an eventful five-year spell, per ESPN's reporting.

Romero's availability comes as Tottenham reshapes its defense. The club signed Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton for 52 million pounds and added Marcos Senesi as a free agent in June. Both moves suggest De Zerbi is willing to refresh the back line.

However, Romero's tenure at Spurs included disciplinary complications that may factor into Inter's final valuation. He served four separate suspensions during the 2025-26 campaign, a pattern that raised questions about his consistency. Ausilo's cautionary language that "these things take some time" also signals that a deal is not yet advanced and substantial negotiations remain ahead.
No official fee has been disclosed, and the open questions around the deal's structure and Romero's personal preference for a move remain unanswered based on available reporting.
